dataset.title: Electricity net imports as % of demand (Ember via OWID)

indicator.name: Electricity net imports (% of demand)
indicator.description: Net electricity imports as a share of demand: Electricity imports minus exports, measured as a percentage of total electricity demand in the country or region.

source.name: Our World in Data – Energy dataset (Ember electricity data)

File owid_energy.csv downloaded from https://catalog.ourworldindata.org/energy/owid_energy/owid_energy.csv on 2026-10-12 19:10 UTC (server Last-Modified: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 14:42:02 GMT).

upstream.name: Ember – Yearly Electricity Data (2026) and Yearly Electricity Data Europe (2026)

notes: Imported from data/raw/owid/owid_energy.csv, column "electricity_net_imports_share_of_demand_pct", years 1990 on (one row per country and year; the latest year with a value is shown, the full series is kept for charts and derived datasets).

Codebook (data/raw/owid/owid_energy.codebook.csv) title: "Net electricity imports as a share of demand"; unit: "%"; sources: Ember – Yearly Electricity Data Europe (2026); Ember – Yearly Electricity Data (2026); Department for Business, Energy & Industrial Strategy of the UK – UK's historical electricity data (2023).

Rows with a blank iso_code are matched by their "country" name: Kosovo -> XKX; regions, income groups and source-defined aggregates (e.g. "Europe (EI)", "G20 (Ember)", "World") and former states are skipped. A blank cell is kept as missing, never 0.
caveats: Grid electricity only: a country that burns imported fuel in its own power plants (e.g. Japan) shows about 0 here. The import exposure adds that channel.

scoring.rationale: A direct import share, but it misses imported fuel burned at home; its positive part is included in the scored import exposure instead (counting it again would double count).
